scenes.say: Ever had your pipeline break because someone changed the data? How can teams prevent these surprises?

scenes.label: Contract
scenes.sub: A formal agreement on schema, quality, and delivery between teams.
scenes.say: A data contract is a formal agreement between data producers and consumers. It spells out the schema, quality, and delivery expectations.
For example, a contract might require customer ID to be an integer, unique, with no missing values, delivered every morning by seven.
Without contracts, teams get unexpected schema changes and broken pipelines. With contracts, everyone knows what to expect, and surprises drop.

scenes.question: Are data contracts only about schemas?
scenes.right: No, they cover schema, quality, and delivery expectations.
scenes.say: Watch out—data contracts aren't just about schemas. They also cover data quality and when the data gets delivered.
